source_document.body:
Pfizer plans to build a $650 million Manufacturing Technology Center at its research and development campus in Groton, Conn., AdvanceCT announced last week.
What’s Related
The roughly 220,000-square-foot facility will manufacture clinical active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug products for Pfizer-sponsored clinical trials worldwide. Construction is set to start in the second quarter of 2027, with operations targeted for mid-2031.
Pfizer will spend $650 million over the next five years, according to AdvanceCT, the state’s nonprofit economic development group.
“Pfizer has a long and proud history of scientific innovation in Groton, where many of the discoveries that advance our pipeline begin. Building on that legacy, the new Manufacturing Technology Center will advance our ability to support clinical research and the development of new medicines for patients around the world,” said Raja Mangipudy, Ph.D., Pfizer’s Groton site head.
Bringing the work under one roof
The project won’t add new jobs . Instead, the center will bring together employees who now work in other buildings across the Groton campus. The project will update the infrastructure behind Pfizer’s current workforce and pull related operations into a new building designed for the company’s future clinical manufacturing needs.
The announcement doesn’t list any state incentives for the project.
The Groton campus covers 175 acres and employs about 2,700 people, according to the Connecticut Business and Industry Association. It has more than 2 million square feet of lab and office space. Pfizer has been in Groton since 1946.
RELATED: Amazon Eyes Second Massive Warehouse in Eastern Connecticut
A major Pfizer research center
Groton is one of Pfizer’s major research centers. The site’s work spans scientific discovery, pharmaceutical sciences, and clinical development, along with the global supply of materials used in clinical research.
“The Manufacturing Technology Center will connect scientific discovery with the advanced manufacturing capabilities needed to support clinical trials around the world,” said John Bourdeaux, president and CEO of AdvanceCT.
State officials called the project a win for Connecticut.
“Pfizer’s investment is an endorsement of the strong momentum across Connecticut’s economy , as companies in a wide range of industries choose to expand , modernize, and make long-term commitments here,” said Daniel O’Keefe, Connecticut’s commissioner of economic development.
Local leaders also welcomed the news.
“This new Manufacturing Technology Center reflects a long-term commitment to our city and the talented people who work here,” said Jill Rusk, mayor of the City of Groton.
